leads.summary: Punctuation-boundary app labels bypass the new label-word classifier
leads.consequence: If a desktop entry is named Google Chrome-Beta, Google Chrome: Beta or Google Chrome™ rather than having a space after Chrome, it matches chr in search but Chrome settings still sorts above the app. The producer forwards arbitrary desktop-entry Name as a string, but the new classifier splits only on whitespace, unlike the existing app-name tokenizer in AppSearch.js, which splits hyphenated names. Parenthesized Google Chrome (Beta) works. This is conditional on these desktop Name spellings; no claim is made that stock Chrome uses them.
leads.triage: covered by Opus (conservative behaviour); synthetic labels only; no stock case

leads.summary: Prototype-name label keys cannot be recorded in appScores
leads.consequence: For a customized action Constructor and an app My Constructor, both matching cons, the action's 10026 score stays ahead of the app's 25027, even though the action is a literal word of the app. appScores.constructor inherits Object.prototype.constructor, so its undefined sentinel is not met, and comparison with the inherited function is false. Rare custom-name case, use an own-key check or prototype-free map for scores.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found in the ranking change; one test gap and overlapping open PRs.

### Source assertion does not pin the pass before the sort

The assertion checks that the call and its wrapper exist, not where the call runs. Moved after the sort, where it cannot change the order, all 126 assertions still pass. **Impact:** a refactor could disable the fix silently.

**Suggested change:** match the call followed by `currentRows.sort(searchSort)` (see reproducer).

<details><summary>Reproducer (passes at 03df5f6 with the call moved after the sort)</summary>

Reviewed head: omacom/omarchy PR #11730 at `03df5f6ed3f0a3707fb9a8aac78e3e96099c92db`.

The new assertion `menu runs the result-set pass over every search row through the shared model` only checks that the text `root.demoteManagementRows(currentRows.concat(drilldownRows))` appears somewhere in `Menu.qml`. Moving that call to after `drilldownRows.sort(searchSort)`, where changing `score` can no longer affect the order, keeps every assertion in `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` passing.

Run from the root of an omarchy checkout at the PR head:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml')
t = p.read_text()
call = "      root.demoteManagementRows(currentRows.concat(drilldownRows))\n"
sort = "      drilldownRows.sort(searchSort)\n"
assert t.count(call) == 1 and t.count(sort) == 1
t = t.replace(call, "").replace(sort, sort + call)
p.write_text(t)
PY
grep -n -B1 'root.demoteManagementRows(currentRows' shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml
bash test/shell.d/menu-test.sh > menu-test.out 2>&1
echo "exit=$?"
echo "ok lines: $(grep -c '^ok - ' menu-test.out), not ok lines: $(grep -c '^not ok - ' menu-test.out)"
grep -E 'directly behind that app|result-set pass' menu-test.out
```

Actual output:

```
650-      drilldownRows.sort(searchSort)
651:      root.demoteManagementRows(currentRows.concat(drilldownRows))
exit=0
ok lines: 126, not ok lines: 0
ok - menu sorts actions labelled with a word of a matching app directly behind that app
ok - menu runs the result-set pass over every search row through the shared model
```

A placement-aware pattern in the same style fails this mutant and still matches the PR head (checked with an equivalent Python `re` pattern against both files):

```js
/root\.demoteManagementRows\(currentRows\.concat\(drilldownRows\)\)[\s\S]*?currentRows\.sort\(searchSort\)/
```
</details>

### Overlap with other open ranking fixes

#12223, #10457 and #9159 change the same ranking incompatibly; #11580 removes the row split this call uses. With #12223 or #10457 merged the new Chrome assertion fails; with #9159 the tests pass but Google Chrome stays behind its Chrome rows. **Impact:** whichever lands second needs rework.

**Suggested change:** link the earlier issue #10340 and these PRs.

<details><summary>Reproducer (#12223 and #9159 merged into 03df5f6)</summary>

Reviewed head: omacom/omarchy PR #11730 at `03df5f6ed3f0a3707fb9a8aac78e3e96099c92db`.
Other heads: #12223 at `b74292ac5992d7c1d6424f85f5456aa8fe1661e6`, #9159 at `4236c8df2c43e797e9e3d31a3c7717a056d80250`.

Both merge into this PR without a textual conflict.

#### #12223 (apps always rank first): this PR's test fails

```bash

git checkout --detach pr-11730 && git merge --no-edit pr-12223
bash test/shell.d/menu-test.sh > menu-test.out 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"

grep '^not ok - ' menu-test.out
```

Actual output:

```

ok lines: 34
not ok - menu sorts actions labelled with a word of a matching app directly behind that app
```

The test stops at its first failure. In a separate run on the `quattro` tip (`8b4eae66`) merged with this PR and #12223, the five new assertions were evaluated one by one (same expressions, same fixture). Three fail: the Chrome, Vim and Browser checks. There Google Chrome scores -69627 for `chr` and Document Viewer -69626 for `vi`, so the apps already outrank every row and the pass never fires. The same three assertions fail with #10457 merged (after resolving its small fixture conflict in `menu-test.sh` (both add an `apps.chrome` row)). Both of those PRs lift installed apps in general, so Document Viewer also ranks above Vim for `vi`.

#### #9159 (usage ranking): tests pass, pass no longer reorders

#9159 replaces the score comparison in `rebuildDisplay()` with `MenuModel.compareSearchRows`, which sorts by `matchPriority` before `score`. On the merged tree `menu-test.sh` still passes, but `chr` no longer lifts Google Chrome.

```bash
git checkout --detach pr-11730 && git fetch origin pull/9159/head:pr-9159 && git merge --no-edit pr-9159
bash test/shell.d/menu-test.sh > menu-test.out 2>&1; echo "menu-test exit=$?"
node with9159.js . | sed -n '/^== /,$p'
```

`with9159.js` (save it in the checkout root) replays the merged query branch of `rebuildDisplay()` for `chr` with Google Chrome installed, no Chromium app and no usage history:

```js
'use strict'

const path = require('path')
const root = process.argv[2]
const M = require(path.join(root, 'shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js'))
const qml = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml'), 'utf8')
const start = qml.indexOf('    if (query) {')
console.log(qml.slice(start, qml.indexOf('rows = currentRows.concat(drilldownRows)', start) + 40))
const merged = M.mergeMenuSources(M.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc'), 'utf8')), [])
const st = M.mergeAppRows(merged.items, merged.itemOrder, [
  { id: 'apps.google-chrome', parent: 'apps', kind: 'app', label: 'Google Chrome', description: 'Web Browser', aliases: ['Web Browser'], order: 0 }
])
const pkgs = new Set(['google-chrome'])
const whenResults = {}, disabledResults = {}
for (const id of st.itemOrder) {
  const it = st.items[id]
  const g = e => { const m = /^omarchy-pkg-present (\S+)$/.exec(e); return m ? pkgs.has(m[1]) : /chromium-flags\.conf ]]$/.test(e) }
  if (it.when) whenResults[id] = g(it.when)
  if (it.disabled) disabledResults[id] = g(it.disabled)
}
for (const [label, pass] of [['without pass', false], ['with pass', true]]) {
  const q = 'chr'
  const cur = [], dd = []

    const entry = st.items[id]

    const visible = M.isVisible(st.items, st.itemOrder, whenResults, entry) && !M.isDisabled(disabledResults, entry)

    row.lastUsedAt = 0
    if (entry.parent === 'root') cur.push(row); else dd.push(row)

  if (pass) M.demoteManagementRows(st.items, cur.concat(dd))
  cur.sort(M.compareSearchRows); dd.sort(M.compareSearchRows)
  console.log(`== "chr" ${label}`)
  cur.concat(dd).slice(0, 6).forEach((r, i) => console.log(`${i + 1}. ${r.path} [priority ${r.matchPriority} score ${r.score}]`))
```

#11580 at `231e4ea8` builds one flat `rows` array in `Menu.qml` (lines 724-896) instead of `currentRows` and `drilldownRows`, and GitHub already reports it as conflicting with `quattro`. Issue #10340 (open) reports the same `chro` ranking bug as #11614.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- `chr` with Google Chrome and no Chromium app gives exactly the before/after order in the PR table.
- With a modelled set of 32 stock Omarchy apps, 873 prefix queries (2 to 6 letters) show no order change; `vi` keeps the Vim rows above Document Viewer.
- The in-place score change through the QML wrapper reorders rows in a Qt 6.11.2 `qml` runtime probe.
- `menu-test.sh` passes at the head (126) and merged onto `quattro` `8b4eae66` (132); the new test fails on base code, and a no-op pass fails the Chrome assertion.

**Optional notes:**
- PR description: "moves one slot" and "both stay in the top five" hold for `tex` and `edg` but not in general. With LibreOffice Writer and Sublime Text installed, `te` moves `Trigger › Capture › Text` from 5th to 7th, because every row scored between the action and the app also moves ahead of it (reproducer below).

Reviewed head: omacom/omarchy PR #11730 at `03df5f6ed3f0a3707fb9a8aac78e3e96099c92db`.

The PR says a non-managing action that shares a word with an installed app "moves one slot, to directly behind that app" and stays in the top five. The action lands behind the app, so every row scored between the two also moves ahead of it. With stock LibreOffice Writer and Sublime Text installed, `te` moves `Trigger › Capture › Text` from 5th to 7th, out of the top five. `tex` behaves as the PR describes.

Save as `te-order.js` in the root of an omarchy checkout at the PR head and run `node te-order.js`:

```js
// Replays the query branch of rebuildDisplay() in shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml
// at the root menu, with the shipped menu, no guard results (every row
// visible, none disabled), and two installed apps (stock LibreOffice Writer
// plus Sublime Text). Prints the first eight rows without and with the pass.
const fs = require('fs')
const menu = require(require('path').resolve('shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js'))
const base = menu.mergeMenuSources(menu.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync('default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc', 'utf8')), [])
const st = menu.mergeAppRows(base.items, base.itemOrder, [
  { id: 'apps.libreoffice-writer', parent: 'apps', kind: 'app', label: 'LibreOffice Writer', description: 'Word Processor', aliases: ['Word Processor'] },
  { id: 'apps.sublime_text', parent: 'apps', kind: 'app', label: 'Sublime Text', description: 'Text Editor', aliases: ['Text Editor'] }
])
function search(query, withPass) {
  const currentRows = [], drilldownRows = []
  for (const id of st.itemOrder) {
    const entry = st.items[id]
    if (!entry || id === 'root') continue
    if (!menu.matchesQuery(entry, query, menu.isVisible(st.items, st.itemOrder, {}, entry))) continue
    const row = menu.displayRow(st.items, st.itemOrder, {}, {}, entry, menu.parentPathFor(st.items, id), menu.searchScore(st.items, entry, query))
    if (entry.parent === 'root') currentRows.push(row); else drilldownRows.push(row)
  }
  if (withPass) menu.demoteManagementRows(st.items, currentRows.concat(drilldownRows))
  const sort = (a, b) => a.score !== b.score ? a.score - b.score : a.path.localeCompare(b.path)
  currentRows.sort(sort); drilldownRows.sort(sort)
  return currentRows.concat(drilldownRows)
}
for (const q of ['te', 'tex']) {
  for (const withPass of [false, true]) {
    console.log(`"${q}" ${withPass ? 'with' : 'without'} the pass:`)
    search(q, withPass).slice(0, 8).forEach((r, i) => console.log(`  ${i + 1}. ${r.path}`))
  }
}
```
